lesson_title: Potential Energy: The Bank Account in the Sky
hook_text: Every water tower is a savings account. Physics does the banking.
clip_script: Every water tower is a savings account on stilts. The pump spends electricity all night pushing water up into the tank — genuine work, paid in full. But the spending is not waste: it is a deposit. The water sits up there holding the energy, and when a tap opens in the morning, the height pays it back as rushing pressure. Work in, storage, work out. That is gravitational potential energy: energy banked by lifting something against gravity. The price of any deposit is the lifting bill: mass times gravitational acceleration times height — the weight, times how high you carried it. Heavier object, steeper bill; higher lift, steeper bill.
visual_style: A water tower filling at night with joule-coins stacking inside the tank, then a morning tap opening and the coins cascading out as rushing water.
pacing: Cosy night-time setup, coin-stack build, satisfying morning payout.
